(1) The interactive PreToolUse gate fix (e678015) made the hook FIRE but it fired into a CRASH: the gate CLI read input.args.file_path while Claude Code's real payload is {hook_event_name,tool_name,tool_input}, so input.args was undefined -> TypeError -> fail-safe block on EVERY write (fail-OPEN became fail-CLOSED-on-everything). 'verified end-to-end' had exercised the internal {tool,args} test shape, never the real wire payload. FIXED: normalizeHookInput adapter accepts both shapes; checkHook + tests now drive the REAL payload and require approve on a non-gated file (a block there = a crashing handler). (2) The headless engineer is gated POST-HOC in-process (gateWorktreeEdits over the worktree diff) — NOT via the interactive hook; the 08:50 'runImplementCli now gates' note was right in spirit but the framing conflated the two boundaries (now corrected in code/comments/RFC). (3) gateWorktreeEdits had two latent fail-opens: it scanned only .ts/.tsx (missed .intent) and used plain 'git status --porcelain' (collapses untracked dirs + quotes special-char paths) -> now shared isGatedFile + 'git status --porcelain -z -uall'. (4) The 08:50 path lesson was misdiagnosed: intents are BEHAVIORAL and must NOT pin paths; the real root was a missing layout SSoT (iaPaths in core-schema) — done.

meta-lesson: a single manual 'I saw it block, therefore it works' verification is not enough for the mechanical boundary — it blocked because it crashed on everything. Empirical tests MUST drive the exact production payload shape (real Claude Code {tool_name,tool_input}), and the doctor (checkHook) must round-trip that shape and require approve on a known-good input, else the diagnostic green-lights a broken gate. Locked with cli.test + checkHook real-shape coverage.
